Three of the words a printed index carries are not written by the author at
all: the heading over the entries that file under no letter, and the two words
in front of a cross-reference. This document and its twin write the same marks
and differ only in whether the metadata above declares those words — so what a
reader sees here is whatever that metadata says, and English wherever it says
nothing.

Nothing below writes a label word. Every mark here is an ordinary one.

## The first index {#site-first}

A term filing under a letter: [Kestrel]{.index}. A term filing under none,
which is what puts a group heading over it: [#numerals]{.index}.

A cross-reference pointing at the first: [Falcon]{.index see="Kestrel"}, and
one pointing further: [Merlin]{.index see-also="Kestrel"}.

## The second index {#site-second}

A term filing under a letter: [Zeppelin]{.index index="authors"}. One filing
under none: [~wavelet]{.index index="authors"}.

Its own two cross-references: [Blimp]{.index index="authors" see="Zeppelin"}
and [Dirigible]{.index index="authors" see-also="Zeppelin"}.
